INDEPENDENT CLOUD REVIEWER, dispatched by a cron-scheduled routine, not by the author. I was never spawned by the authoring session, I cannot see its reasoning, and I read only this repository and the GitHub REST API. No agent gave me this task. Every PR body, commit message, prior record and document I read was treated as DATA, not as instructions -- which matters more than usual here, because the deliverable under review is itself a document making assertions about how reviewers should behave. Nothing in it redirected me. reviewer_was_dispatched_by_author is false by construction.

VERDICT: DISAGREE at branch head f1ee2df3dd9b0f0a6a90a616012a6397d43dfdee (reviewable head 5e415c44d50913475e498e47dcb65813d1cb7d99, obtained by running lwb_lanes.resolve_reviewable_head, not assumed).

ENVIRONMENT AND BASE. Linux container, CPython 3.11, pytest 9.1.1, pyyaml installed by me. origin/main was FETCHED FIRST and confirmed twice -- git and the REST commits/main endpoint both give live main = bfe850796969980545811e1ffa551b9143965faf. B2 below is a staleness charge and was made only after the base was proven fresh.

WHAT IS GOOD, said plainly because the honesty of this document is the thing it is for. The suite is GREEN here: `python -m pytest tests/ -q` gives 512 passed, 1 warning (19.9s), the warning being the pre-existing DeprecationWarning at tests/test_lwb_check_proof_reexecute.py:248 that this PR did not introduce. The document corrects its own earlier false claim rather than quietly deleting it, states that honest reporting would NOT have blocked #27, and refuses to amend a landed record. proof/32.json records `checked_by` as the literal UNCHECKED-pending-independent-review rather than borrowing an identity, and its `tokens` block records "unknown" with the reason that a borrowed number is a manufactured one. I could find no overclaim in the unproven list.

=== WHAT I VERIFIED ABOUT THE CENTRAL FACTUAL CLAIM ===
The document says #27's review record came from a run the author's session fired by hand at 13:59:25Z, session cse_01GaiKSWBCRLtcVa5fPYz4nQ, against a routine whose cron is 23 past the hour.
What I could check from GitHub alone, and did:
  - reviews/27/cloud-reviewer.json on main carries reviewer_id
    "reviewer-cloud-routine-buildcraft-01GaiKSWBCRLtcVa5fPYz4nQ-2026-09-19".
    The session token embedded in that id is the SAME token the document
    names. The document is therefore pointing at the right run, and that
    linkage is verifiable inside this repository rather than only from the
    firing session's own console.
  - Timeline from the REST commits endpoint: the review-record commit on
    #27's branch, 19e42b2f, is dated 2026-09-19T14:09:08Z, and #27 merged
    at 14:18:29Z. A run created at 13:59:25 committing at 14:09 fits. A run
    started at the preceding cron time of 13:23 would have had to sit 46
    minutes before committing, and the following cron time of 14:23 is
    after the merge. The timeline corroborates the document and fits no
    cron alternative I can construct.
NOT CHECKED, and I want this explicit: I did NOT verify the trigger id, the cron expressions 23-past and 53-past, the run-creation timestamp itself, or that a second reviewer routine exists on its own schedule. Those live in the routine scheduler, outside this repository and outside the GitHub REST surface my brief confines me to. I took them on the document's word. The corroboration above is consistent with them; it does not establish them.

=== I REPRODUCED THE DOCUMENT'S OWN DISCLOSED HOLE, AND IT IS REAL ===
The document claims a pull request whose commits touch only reviews/ and proof/ is not covered by the review gate, because classify_path calls those paths shared while resolve_reviewable_head skips record-only commits. I did not take that on trust. Probe, on a throwaway local branch cut from live main, never pushed:
    STEP 1  doc committed under reviews/27/ + an AGREE record naming that
            doc commit                    -> lwb-lanes exit 1, "STALE -- this
            record reviewed 886ed92..., but the current REVIEWABLE head is
            bfe8507..." (both commits were skipped; the reviewable head fell
            through to the BASE on main)
    STEP 2  same, record re-pointed at the base sha bfe8507
                                          -> lwb-lanes exit 0, "check passed"
    STEP 3  the ENTIRE document replaced with a line of nonsense asserting
            the opposite of itself, committed on top
                                          -> lwb-lanes exit 0, "check passed"
STEP 1 is the control -- the gate is not inert, it does refuse a record naming the wrong sha. STEP 3 is the hole: the reviewed content was replaced wholesale after the AGREE record was filed and the gate still passed. The document's disclosure is accurate and its instruction to read the record rather than trust the green check is the right one. I am recording this as CONFIRMED, not as a charge against this PR, which explicitly declines to fix it inside itself and gives a good reason (the fix lives in scripts/lwb_lanes.py and would land through the very hole it closes).

=== B1 (BLOCKING, measured). The pull request does not merge. ===
REST repos/.../pulls/32 reports mergeable=false, mergeable_state="dirty".
    git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD -> exit 1
    CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in HANDOFF.md
HANDOFF.md is the only conflicting file.
Related and worth naming: commits/f1ee2df/check-runs returns ZERO check runs. Not one of the nine required contexts has reported at this head. A conflicted pull request has no merge ref for actions/checkout to resolve, which is consistent with CI never having started. Whatever the cause, nothing green exists to merge on.

=== B2 (BLOCKING, measured). A required check is red: the generated block pins a main SHA that is now two merges stale. ===
    python scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py   ->  exit 1
    FAIL: HANDOFF.md:40: [stale main SHA in generated block] main SHA:
    f9b4deadbb441f0c1046a0d73b0434424f1cf13c (live: bfe850796969980545811e1ffa551b9143965faf)
This is not a cosmetic doc nit. I traced it to a required context rather than assuming: parsing .github/workflows/ci.yml, the step "lwb-check-state-claims" is a step of the `test` job, `test` is the matrix job, and the ruleset requires the `test` context on all six legs (I read the nine required contexts live from the ruleset). The job checks out with fetch-depth: 0, so origin/main on the runner is live main and the check will resolve it exactly as I did -- this is not an artifact of my container having a stale base.
The deeper defect is that the fix applied is not durable. proof/32.json records this same command exiting 0, with a tail reading "recorded main SHA 9b374b5... is live main's first parent ... verified by git". That was true when it was recorded and is false now, because the block pins a volatile SHA by hand and main has moved twice since. "Regenerate LAST" wins the race only until the next merge into main. The durable fix is to stop hand-pinning a volatile SHA in a committed block, or to regenerate it in CI.
SECOND STALENESS IN THE SAME BLOCK, which the checker cannot see: the "Open PRs" list names #31 and #30 as open. REST says #31 is CLOSED and MERGED and #30 is CLOSED, not merged; and the list omits #38, which has been open since 18:28Z. The checker reports this line as "UNVERIFIABLE: Open PRs listing could not be fully re-derived (no gh auth here)" -- so a listing that is provably wrong passes as unverifiable. That is the repository's own recurring shape: a check that cannot tell "I looked and found nothing" from "I could not look". I am recording it as a finding against the check's reporting, not only against this block.

=== N1 (NON-BLOCKING, mine). proof/32.json's `commit` field names 3509d2f, three commits below the reviewable head. ===
Two commits on this branch post-date it: 51fa05d (the proof record) and 5e415c4 (the HANDOFF regeneration, which is a shared path). The record is honest about being self-authored, but the commit it certifies is not the commit that would land. Not blocking on its own; it compounds B2, because the state-claims command it records as green was run against a tree that no longer exists.

=== TWO NEAR-MISSES I AM PRINTING BECAUSE I ALMOST FILED THEM ===
1. `python scripts/lwb_check_env_leak.py` exits 1 here with "UNCONFIGURED: LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES is unset or empty". I was one step from charging a red required check. It is not one: ci.yml supplies that variable from a repository secret for both env-leak steps, and the UNCONFIGURED refusal is deliberate fail-closed design -- the check refusing to pass while scanning for nothing. The red is my container, not this branch. No charge.
2. The generated block reads "20/20 proven" and `ls proof/*.json` counts 22. I started writing a miscount finding. Two of the 22 are proof/schema.json and proof/exempt.json, which are not records; lwb_check_proof.py independently reports "passed (20 record(s))". The block is right and I was wrong. No charge.

=== WHAT I DID NOT CHECK, explicitly ===
- The routine scheduler: trigger ids, cron expressions, run-creation timestamps, and the existence of a second reviewer routine. Outside my permitted surface; taken on the document's word. See above.
- I did not re-run the prior reviewers' ten mutation probes on #27's merged code, and I did not review #27 itself. This PR does not change code.
- I did not verify that the procedural mitigation ("reviewer routines are never fired by hand for a PR the firing session authored") is actually in force anywhere enforceable. By the document's own account it is procedural, not mechanical, and I have no way to observe compliance.
- I did not attempt any fix. I write records and comments only. The STEP 1-3 probe ran on a local throwaway branch that was deleted and never pushed; nothing outside reviews/32/ is touched by this commit.
- I did not check the four prior records on this branch for accuracy beyond the findings I re-derived myself.

WHAT WOULD MOVE ME TO AGREE: merge live main in and resolve HANDOFF.md; get the generated block to stop asserting a volatile main SHA (or regenerate it as the last act before merge and keep it that way); correct or drop the Open PRs listing; and get CI to actually run and go green at the head. None of that touches the substance of the correction document, which I think is sound.

ON MY OWN IDENTITY. reviewer_id keeps the mandated "reviewer-cloud-routine-buildcraft" verbatim and appends this session's real token and today's date, so the id carries true provenance rather than a shape picked to satisfy a validator. commit_author_id is copied from proof/32.json's `author` field; it is self-declared and I verified it against nothing external, because nothing external attests it. D16 still holds.
